 Oral Judgment
The Tribunal passed a common judgment in MVC Nos.199/2014 and 200/2014.
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 06.09.2017 passed by the I Additional District Judge and MACT, Raichur, in MVC No.199 of 2014.

entities.text: I Additional District Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts of the case are that, on 21.09.2013, while the claimant along with other villagers were proceeding in an auto from Yeragera to Kasbe Camp for coolie work, the driver of the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-36/TB-8536 attached with trolley driven it in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed to the auto, due to which, claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Therefore, he filed a claim petition NC: 2025:KHC-K:6489 HC-KAR before the Tribunal,
claiming compensation of Rs.18,50,000/-.

3. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.3,45,450/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, he was doing agricultural and coolie work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal erred in taking his income at Rs.5,000/- per month; the Doctor has assessed the disability at 60% to the whole body, but the Tribunal has taken the disability only at 25%; he spent Rs.2,00,000/- for his treatment, but the lesser amount was granted under the head 'medical expenses'; the amount awarded under other heads is meagre and no amount was granted for expenses towards artificial limb NC: 2025:KHC-K:6489 HC-KAR and loss of income during laid Narayana vs Venkatesh G And Anr on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48984416/
2 up period.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6.
Though the appellant contended that he was doing coolie work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.
Hence, as he met with an accident in the year 2013, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.7,000/- per month.

7. As it is a case of amputation, as per the citation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the dictum of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1, 10% of the income is to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, his monthly income comes to Rs.7,700/- (7,000 + 10%).
8.
The doctor assessed the disability at 60%.
It is a case of amputation of right leg below knee.

Considering (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6489 HC-KAR the nature of injury and the occupation of the appellant, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 60%.
9.
Considering the age of the appellant as 50 years, the multiplier of 13 adopted by the Tribunal is just and proper.

10. Thus, the loss of future earnings comes to Rs.7,700 x 12 x 13 x 60% = Rs.7,20,720/-
11.
The Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.31,450/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.

12. Considering the nature of injuries, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.50,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
13. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of six months due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, he is entitled for an NC: 2025:KHC-K:6489 HC-KAR amount of Rs.42,000/- (Rs.7,000 x 6) for loss of income during laid up period.
14. He is also entitled for an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- for fixation of artificial limb.

15. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.31,450/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.7,20,720 Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of income during laid up period Rs.42,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
Artificial limb Rs.2,00,000/-

Enhancement Rs.8,28,720/-
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.8,28,720/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

16. In the result, the following order is passed:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6489 HC-KAR (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.8,28,720/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

However, as per the orders on I.A.1/2025 dated 25.09.2025 and I.A.2/2025 dated 03.11.2025, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 1952 days in filing the appeal and in recall application respectively.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
